findings.text: Named indirect call points can be declared with a normal initial target, an empty initial target, or an initial target that yields zero, together with a conditional invocation helper that tolerates an empty target. Relevant identifiers include DEFINE_STATIC_CALL plus null and return zero variants and static_call_cond.
In the shown configurations the initialized indicator stays false, the init helper reports success while doing nothing, and the text reservation check reports no reservation.

One target updater changes the recorded destination while holding CPU hotplug read protection across the store and the architecture specific patch step. A second updater only records the new destination with no extra synchronization visible in the fragment.
A call site record pairs two signed offsets, one for the patched location and one for its key.

A call key always records the current destination. One layout adds a union that can hold a numeric tag or patch metadata linkage, with the lowest bit selecting the interpretation. Other layouts record only the destination.

Key and trampoline symbols use different name prefixes with stringified and length forms available. Site tags use value one for tail calls and value two for init section sites, with value three as the combined mask.

Visibility helpers expose keys and trampolines to modules in standard and GPL restricted forms. One form exposes both key and trampoline, a minimal form exposes only the key, and dedicated forms expose only the trampoline.

Conditional dispatch observes the current destination once and substitutes a no operation routine when empty. One addressability mode keeps the key reachable for patch tracking while another resolves directly to the trampoline.

Platform suspend control uses a table covering validation and begin, early and late preparation, entry and wake, finish and end, plus a repeat query and a recovery hook. An idle focused table covers begin and preparation, late preparation and checking, a wake query, early and full restore, and end.
Platform hibernation control uses a table covering begin and end, snapshot preparation and finish, image preparation and entry, leaving, restore preparation and cleanup, and recovery.
Hibernation page bookkeeping chains entries that associate a copy location with the original page location.
Suspend states are ordered as working zero, idle one, standby two, memory three, with an upper bound of four. Minimum suspend equals idle.

Idle suspend moves among not suspended, entering and waking, with an entering only predicate. Suspend progress steps run from working through freeze and prepare, then suspend with late and no interrupt phases, then no interrupt resume with early resume and final resume.

Global flags track firmware driven suspend, firmware driven resume, and no platform mode. Helpers clear all flags, set each one, and query each one. A disabled configuration reports all queries false and keeps the target state at working, so the in progress predicate stays false.

Suspend and hibernate services install platform tables, start transitions, manage no save regions and page markers, and report availability and progress. Disabled variants do nothing on install, report not supported on start, and report false for availability and progress while keeping sync on suspend enabled.
Power notification phases are numbered one through six for hibernate prepare and completion, suspend prepare and completion, restore prepare, and restore failure.

Coordination services cover notifier registration, hardware sleep reporting, allocation mask restriction, sync assistance, wake pending checks and signaling, and sleep locking. Disabled variants succeed trivially on registration, report no wake pending, return zero from lock, and report no transition in progress.

A bounce pool describes an address interval with its virtual mapping, slab and area counts, area table and slot table, and late allocation marking. Dynamic builds add list linkage with deferred free work plus transient and shared markers.

Bounce state holds a default pool with total slab count, a debug handle, and flags for forced bouncing and allocation or shared use. Dynamic builds add growth permission with a physical limit, a pool list and allocation work. Debug builds add counters for total use with high water and transient slabs.

Initialization flags select verbose setup and unrestricted memory use. Segment size is one hundred twenty eight with slot shift eleven. Default size is configuration driven in one build and sixty four megabytes in the other.

Pool lookup yields nothing when bounce state is absent, accepts addresses inside the default interval, and in dynamic mode uses a fuller search when bounce use is indicated. Unmap and device or processor sync helpers delegate inward only when a pool is found. Force bounce and allocation use checks reflect device state.

Disabled bounce builds do nothing for init and exit and size adjustment, always find no pool, report inactive and unallocated, allow unlimited mapping size, report zero base and limit, and report allocation as unavailable.
Trace export entries chain through a protected link, carry a write hook taking an entry with a buffer and length, and flag bits for function and event and marker export.

Array message emission records the caller address with the string when present and reports negative one otherwise. Console and terminal switch helpers do nothing here. Power logging prefixes output and gates debug messages by runtime checks, discarding them in the disabled build.
Observing bounce use and pool membership after loading a driver supplied address needs ordering against concurrent allocation path updates, otherwise a cross processor check can miss membership.
Dynamic bounce state colocates a spinlock with the pool list and growth controls, indicating serialized changes to the pool set.
